teaser: He left home to kill the Prophet ﷺ and came back testifying. After that, Muslims prayed openly.
quran_mention: He is not named in the Qur'an. The ayah that broke him was in Surah Taha: «إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدْنِي وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ لِذِكْرِي» — 'Indeed I am Allah. There is no god but Me, so worship Me and establish the prayer to remember Me.' (20:14)

layers.title: Who He Was
layers.subtitle: The camel-herd's son who frightened grown men
layers.content:
Umar ibn al-Khattab ibn Nufayl ibn Abd al-Uzza ibn Rabah ibn Abdullah ibn Qurt ibn Razzah ibn Adi ibn Ka'b. His kunya was Abu Hafs. His mother was Hantama bint Hashim ibn al-Mughira, of Banu Makhzum. He said of himself: 'I was born four years before the Great al-Fijar.'

His family's house in Makka stood at the base of a mountain the Arabs called al-Aqir. It is called Jabal Umar today. Ibn Sa'd asked a scholar of Makkan affairs where the man had lived, and that was the answer.

Years later, riding past the ravine of Dajnan as caliph, he stopped. 'I remember when I used to herd camels for al-Khattab here. By Allah, I know that he was a coarse harsh person. Sometimes I gathered wood for them and sometimes I worked for them.' Then, quietly: 'Then I became in charge of the community of Muhammad.' He recited a line of verse about wealth and children perishing, and told his camel to go on.

Those who saw him remembered height first. 'I did not see Umar with a people ever but that I saw that he was taller than them.' Reports describe him white inclining to red, bald, grey. He wrestled in the market of Ukaz. Amr ibn Maymun confessed he never dared pray in the front row: 'He was an awe-inspiring man.'
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Conversion
layers.subtitle: He went out with a sword and came back a believer
layers.content:
Anas ibn Malik narrated it. Umar went out with his sword girded on. A man of Banu Zuhra asked where he was going. 'I am going to kill Muhammad.' The man told him to look closer to home: his own sister and her husband had left the religion of Quraysh.

He found them reciting Surah Taha, with Khabbab hiding inside the house. He knocked his brother-in-law flat. His sister came between them and he struck her until her face bled. Bleeding, she said it anyway: 'Umar, the truth is other than your religion. I testify that there is no god but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.'

Something gave way. 'Give me this book so that I can read it.' She refused him — 'You are impure, and only the purified touch it' — so he washed. He read until he reached «إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنَا» — 'Indeed I am Allah. There is no god but Me.' Then: 'Take me to Muhammad.'

The Prophet ﷺ was in the house at the foot of Safa. He came out, took hold of Umar's garment and sword-belt, and made the supplication he had already made: 'O Allah, exalt Islam by Umar ibn al-Khattab.' Umar testified. Then he said something no one else had dared say: 'Go public, Messenger of Allah.'
layers.quran_ref: Quran 20:14 — 'Indeed I am Allah. There is no god but Me, so worship Me and establish the prayer to remember Me'
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet ﷺ supplicated: 'O Allah, exalt Islam with the one of two men You love most: Umar ibn al-Khattab or Amr ibn Hisham' — narrated by Ibn Umar, Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley (narration of Anas ibn Malik)

layers.title: With the Prophet ﷺ
layers.subtitle: The day the Muslims stopped hiding their prayer
layers.content:
Reports differ on how many had entered Islam before him: forty men and ten women, or about forty in the house of al-Arqam, or forty-five men and eleven women. What the narrators agree on is what changed. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: 'It was only when Umar became Muslim that Islam was made public in Makka.'

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud put it in three clauses: 'Umar's becoming Muslim was an opening, his Hijra was a victory, and his emirate was a mercy. I remember when we could not pray at the House until Umar became Muslim. When Umar became Muslim, he fought them until they let us pray.'

He emigrated by appointment, not by stealth alone — he, Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'a and Hisham ibn al-As agreed to meet at the thorn-trees of Ida'a. Hisham was detained and tortured. In Quba, when Abu Jahl came to coax Ayyash home with news of his mother's vow, Umar warned him plainly: 'By Allah, they will make you revert from your deen. Guard your deen.' Ayyash went, and was bound and imprisoned in Makka.

He was present at Badr, Uhud, the Ditch and every battle. At Khaybar the Prophet ﷺ gave him the banner. Once, granting him leave for umra, the Prophet ﷺ called after him: 'My brother, give me some of your supplication, and do not forget me.'
layers.hadith_ref: At Khaybar the Prophet ﷺ gave the banner to Umar — narrated by Burayda al-Aslami, Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Trial
layers.subtitle: Ten years of holding power and refusing it
layers.content:
Abu Bakr appointed him, and people came to the dying caliph to object. He answered: 'By Allah, are you trying to frighten me? I will say that I appointed the best of them over them.'

Umar's own accounting of what public wealth he was allowed to touch was itemised: 'Two robes are lawful to me, one in the summer and one in the winter, an animal on which to perform hajj and umra, and my food and the food of my family with the food of a middling man of Quraysh, neither rich nor poor. After that I am a man of the Muslims who gets what they get.' He said he stood toward the property of Allah as toward the property of an orphan. Ill once, prescribed honey, he climbed the minbar to ask the community's permission to take a pot of it from the treasury — otherwise, he said, it was unlawful for him.

In the famine year his skin darkened. He had been a man of ghee and milk; he refused them while people starved, ate oil instead, and often went hungry.

Hafsa, his own daughter, once suggested softer food and better clothes now that Allah had expanded provision. He answered her by describing the hard life the Prophet ﷺ endured, until she wept. On the minbar he prayed: 'O Allah, I am harsh, so make me flexible. I am weak, so strengthen me. I am miserly, so make me generous.'
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: Wounded before dawn, and still asking about the prayer
layers.content:
Abu Lu'lu'a, a slave of al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, hid in a corner of the mosque before Fajr with a two-headed dagger. Umar came out to straighten the rows. The man stabbed him three times; the blow below the navel was the fatal one. He wounded a dozen others, then killed himself. Umar stretched out his hand: 'Look out for the dog. It has killed me.'

Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf led the prayer with the two shortest surahs. Umar lost consciousness. When light came he opened his eyes and asked one question: 'Have the people prayed?' Told yes, he said, 'There is no Islam for the one who misses the prayer,' called for water, made wudu, and prayed. Learning his killer had never prostrated to Allah, he said: 'Praise be to Allah who did not make my killer argue with me in the presence of Allah with any prostration he has made.'

He had sent his son to ask Aisha for a grave beside the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr, then feared she had agreed only out of deference to his office. So he left instructions: carry me to her door and ask again. They did. She said, 'Enter with peace.'

His rule lasted ten years, five months and twenty-one days. He left the succession to a council of six rather than name a man.
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley (narrations of Amr ibn Maymun and Ibn Abbas)

quiz.prompt: What was Umar carrying when he set out on the day he became Muslim?

options.text: A written oath from Quraysh
His sword, girded on
A bag of dirhams to bribe the Muslims
Nothing — he was on his way to trade

quiz.citation: Narration of Anas ibn Malik — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He carried a sword to end Islam and put it down to enter it. The distance between those two moments was one page of Surah Taha.

quiz.prompt: Which surah were his sister and brother-in-law reciting when Umar walked in?

options.text: Surah Yasin
Surah al-Fatihah
Surah Taha
Surah Maryam

quiz.citation: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III — the account of Umar's Islam
quiz.scholar_reflection: He read until he reached 'Indeed I am Allah. There is no god but Me' (20:14). He had come to argue and found nothing left to argue with.

quiz.prompt: According to Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, what changed for the Muslims of Makka once Umar accepted Islam?

options.text: Quraysh lifted the boycott of Banu Hashim
They were finally able to pray at the Ka'bah
The migration to Abyssinia was cancelled
Abu Jahl was expelled from Makka

quiz.citation: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, reported in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Ibn Mas'ud said: 'I remember when we could not pray at the House until Umar became Muslim. When Umar became Muslim, he fought them until they let us pray.'

quiz.prompt: What did Umar say was lawful for him personally to take from the public treasury?

options.text: A tenth of everything that entered it
Nothing at all, in any circumstance
Two robes, a mount for hajj and umra, and food at the level of a middling Qurayshi
Whatever the council of the Muhajirun voted him each year

quiz.citation: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III — narrated by al-Ahnaf
quiz.scholar_reflection: He added the sentence that mattered: 'After that I am a man of the Muslims who gets what they get.' He put himself last in the line he controlled.

quiz.prompt: What was the first thing Umar asked about after regaining consciousness from his fatal wound?

options.text: Whether the people had prayed
Who would succeed him
Whether the armies in Persia had held
Whether his attacker had been caught

quiz.citation: Narration of Ibn Abbas — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Told that they had, he said, 'There is no Islam for the one who misses the prayer,' called for water, made wudu, and prayed while bleeding.

quiz.prompt: Umar was on his way to commit a murder when the truth reached him. What does that say about people you have written off?

options.text: No one is past reach — I just rarely act like it
The loudest opponents often have the most conviction to redirect
I quietly sort people into reachable and hopeless
I believe it in principle but not about anyone specific

quiz.citation: Reflection on the account of Umar's Islam, Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Prophet ﷺ named Umar and Abu Jahl in the same supplication, asking for whichever of the two Allah loved more. He did not assume the answer.

quiz.prompt: His sister declared her faith with her face bleeding from his hand. When has holding your position cost you something with family?

options.text: Often — and it has strained things badly
I soften what I believe to keep the peace at home
It has never really been tested
I hold firm, but I am not sure I do it kindly

quiz.citation: Reflection on the narration of Anas ibn Malik, Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Her words were what broke him, not the argument he came to win. There is no judgement here — the cost of speaking honestly at home is real.

quiz.prompt: Umar itemised exactly what he was allowed to take, then took less. What does your own honesty look like when nobody is auditing?

options.text: I take what is permitted and do not think much further
I set my own limit tighter than the rule
I am careful when watched and looser when not
I have never had to decide — nothing has been in my hands

quiz.citation: Reflection on Umar's account of lawful wealth, Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He climbed a minbar to ask permission for a pot of honey while ill. The scale of the thing was small. The habit behind it was not.

quiz.prompt: He refused ghee and milk while the people were hungry, and his skin changed colour from the food he ate instead. Where does solidarity end for you?

options.text: I give from my comfort but keep the comfort
I would go without if the people around me were
I think suffering on purpose helps no one
I have never been close enough to hunger to know

quiz.citation: Reflection on the famine year, Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: When Hafsa urged him toward ease, he answered by describing the Prophet's hardship until she wept. He was not performing austerity. He was refusing to eat alone.

quiz.prompt: He asked Aisha for a grave beside the Prophet ﷺ, then feared she had only agreed because he was caliph — so he made them ask again after his death. What is that fear?

options.text: A man who knew exactly how much power distorts a yes
Scrupulousness about a favour he wanted very badly
Fear that the honour would be unearned
All of it — this is what taqwa looks like in office

quiz.citation: Narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: They carried him to her door and said, 'This is Umar asking permission.' She answered, 'Enter with peace.' He got what he wanted, but only after removing his own thumb from the scale.
